findings.title: AUSE of u_ale mostly scores the tau_min gate, and the paper does not say so
findings.where: usplat/seg_eval.py:335-359 (undefined_key, ranking_signals); usplat/seg_eval.py:382-384 (summarize); scripts/make_tables.py:26-28 (AUSE_u = u_ale for ours); papers/main.tex:680-682 (metrics text), :727-729 (Table I caption), :877-880 (Table III caption); fig:views text
findings.problem: Every AUSE of an own channel ranks pixels in 3 tiers: uncovered, then undefined (NaN), then finite values. For our u_ale, 'undefined' means the pixel is dominated by Gaussians with support < 3 views. So the AUSE_u of u_ale in Table I, the u_ale curves of Fig. views and the 'ale' column of Table III put the low-support pixels first as a tied block. This measures the support gate (an epistemic signal), not rho_hat. CSS variance and the NormLift scores are always defined, so they never get this tier. The paper says only that uncovered pixels rank as most uncertain (main.tex:680-682). It does not say that undefined u_ale ranks above every defined value.
findings.failure_scenario: 1) Table I: synthetic pixels through the real summarize() path, with u_ale set to pure noise. 10% undefined pixels (error 0.40 vs 0.18) give our AUSE_u 15.60, while an always-defined noise channel gets 17.53 (random gap 17.56). The column would show a 2-point 'win' for ours that comes only from the gate. 2) Fig. views and Table III: on the real fields, u_ale is defined for only about 3.6% (office_0) and 7.0% (room_2) of the pixel mass at M=10, and about 35-39% at M=30. So at M=10 almost every covered pixel falls in one tied undefined block. The u_ale curve there says nothing about rho_hat. The rbar / joint / legacy estimator rows of Table III share the same gate, so their 'ale' values, averaged over the 10/30/90 fields, are diluted toward the same number. The 'pixels' variant gates on pixel mass instead, so its tiers differ. Because the low-support block is mostly reducible error, the gate can also make u_ale look like it ranks e_red, which confounds the separation claim. The per-pixel arrays are not saved, so a gate-free AUSE cannot be computed after the test run without a second test run.
findings.evidence:
Code: seg_eval.py:357 `key = torch.where(torch.isfinite(u), u, torch.full_like(u, undefined_key(u)))` (undefined ranks above every finite u). summarize() uses only this key (seg_eval.py:383). No defined-only variant exists (grep for undefined="drop" finds it only in evaluation.py).
Command: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" PYTHONPATH=. python3 scratchpad/ause_gate.py -> `full map (M=180): undefined 10% | AUSE_u ours (3-tier, as Tab I) 15.60 | ours on defined pixels only 15.92 | noise channel always defined 17.53 | random gap 17.56`; `M=30: undefined 60% | 18.35 | 17.43 | 23.59 | 23.57`; `M=10: undefined 95% | 24.74 | 17.39 | 26.80 | 26.72`.
Command: python3 scratchpad/gate_share.py office_0 room_2 (real saved fields, W1(M) ~ W1*M/179) -> office_0 `M=10: 0.1% of Gaussians, 3.6% of pixel mass; M=30: 2.9%, 34.5%; M=90: 12.7%, 69.7%; M=179: 22.4%, 84.2%`; room_2 `M=10: 7.0%; M=30: 39.3%; M=90: 69.7%; M=179: 81.8%` of pixel mass.
findings.fix: Decide before the test run, because the per-pixel data are not kept. (a) In summarize(), also compute each own channel's AUSE on one shared pixel set: covered pixels where our u_ale is defined, the same set for the CSS / NormLift channels. Or save the per-pixel arrays (correct, covered, u channels, conf) of the test scenes so any variant can be computed later. (b) In the Metrics text and the Table I / Table III / Fig. views captions, state that an undefined u_ale ranks above every defined value. Print the undefined share, which is already in the JSON as ranking[...]['n_undefined']. (c) For Fig. views and Table III 'ale', report AUSE on the defined pixels and give the defined share next to it. At M=10, a single tied block holds about 95% of the pixels.

findings.title: eval_seg.py saves no metrics until every scene is done, so one crash loses the whole test run
findings.where: scripts/eval_seg.py:540-554 (run: rec.add only after the scene loop); scripts/eval_seg.py:544-548 (the per-scene print has no Brier/AURC/AUSE)
findings.problem: All per-scene results stay in memory. RunRecord gets them only after the last scene, and the per-scene log line prints only mIoU/acc/ECE/NLL/coverage. If the one-shot test run crashes on a later scene, the finished scenes' Brier, AURC and AUSE are lost, and the test run must be repeated.
findings.failure_scenario: The 6-scene test run finishes room_0..office_3, then gets a CUDA OOM on office_4 when a USGLoc job starts, as happened on val at 20:16. eval_test.json then has metrics = {}. Table I needs Brier, AURC and AUSE_u, so the test scenes must be evaluated a second time.
findings.evidence: The val run of 20:13 finished office_0 (lines in stage_val.log) and then hit an OOM on room_2 (stage_val.log traceback: `torch.OutOfMemoryError ... frozen_on ... share`, `exit 1 2026-09-29 20:16:31`). Command: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/home/thanhnc/gauss_ws/data/uags_results/tab1/eval_val.json')); print(d['metrics'].keys())" -> `dict_keys([])`. The office_0 metrics are lost except the printed lines, which is why logs/eval_val_partial_2013.log had to be rebuilt from a transcript.
findings.fix: Write each scene's result as soon as it finishes. Either call rec.add(f"scene_{name}", result) inside the loop, or write <out>.<scene>.json. Add a --skip-done option that reloads finished scenes, so a crash resumes the same frozen evaluation instead of repeating it.

findings.title: Near-zero-evidence Gaussians: mu* is not unit and the support is 0 instead of W1
findings.where: usplat/vmf_field.py:613-614 (mu_post = F.normalize(kappa_hat*R), eps 1e-12); usplat/vmf_field.py:191-198 (kish() returns 0 when W2 < 1e-12, so support = min(0, W1) = 0)
findings.problem: The paper defines mu* = R/||R|| and s = W1. For Gaussians with W1 < ~3e-6, kappa_hat is clamped to 1e-6, so ||kappa_hat R|| < 1e-12. F.normalize then returns a vector shorter than 1 (min 0.17). W2 < 1e-12 makes kish = 0, so support = 0 and u_epi = 1 instead of 1/(1+W1).
findings.failure_scenario: There is no measurable effect on Table I: these Gaussians hold less than 3e-11 of the pixel mass. It is a silent departure from the stated definitions, and it could matter for a map with many near-invisible Gaussians or a smaller a0.
findings.evidence: Command: python3 scratchpad/field_stats.py office_0 room_2 -> office_0 `support < W1 (min binds): 1728; kish==0 while W1>0: 1728, their max W1 2.94e-06`, `P0 |mu*| on seen: min 0.1736 #(<0.999) 332`; room_2 `2729 ... max W1 2.99e-06`, `#(<0.999) 579`. gate_share.py -> `|mu*|<0.999 on 332 seen Gaussians: max W1 1.25e-07, pixel-mass share 1.57e-11` (room_2: 579, 2.74e-11).
findings.fix: Compute mu* as R/||R|| (clamped) when prior_kappa = 0. In views mode, use support = W1, or compute kish with a relative epsilon (W2 > 0) instead of the absolute 1e-12.

checked_ok: Tests: tests/test_estimators.py + tests/test_legacy.py: 11 passed. test_seg_eval, test_state, test_baselines, test_ablation_rows, test_view_count: 44 passed (CPU, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="").
The saved val fields (office_0, room_2) were made with the paper's defaults: evidence=views, estimator=kish, epistemic=support, tau_min=3, c0=1, kappa_mode=map, prior_kappa=0, centre off, float32.
Support: W2 <= W1 holds for every Gaussian in both fields, so min(n_K, W1) = W1, as the paper states (s = W1). The only exception is the near-zero case in the minor finding.

rho_hat (eq:rho): the code matches the paper. The clamp at 1 can never bind (||R||^2 - Q <= W1^2 - W2, because ||u|| <= 1). On the real fields no Gaussian is clamped at 0 or 1. u_ale is defined for 22.4% / 12.2% of Gaussians, ranges [6e-5, 0.101] / [4e-5, 0.089], mean 0.0195 / 0.0069. This matches logs/support_stats.log. Within-view ||u|| is 0.9996, so the tiny u_ale is real and not a numerical artefact.

Joint-prior kappa_hat: A_d(kappa_hat) = ||R||/(W1 + c0) and kappa_post = kappa_hat ||R||, as the paper states. The A_d table matches mpmath (worst relative error 2.9e-6 over kappa 1e-6..3e7, continuous at the CF/scipy switch, kappa = 31). a_d_inv round trip is exact to about 1e-8. The float32 clamp 1 - 1e-9 rounds to 1, but r <= 179/180 so it never matters.

P1 = A_d(kappa_post) mu* shrinks as the paper says. Pixel-mass-weighted mean |E mu| is 0.923 (office_0) and 0.902 (room_2). It is 0.002 for W1 < 0.1, 0.73 for W1 in [1,3) and 0.995 for W1 >= 10. All buffers are finite.

P2 beta cannot blow up or go negative with the frozen val parameters. a = 0.36, b = 11.8 and g = 0.055 are all > 0, rendered u_epi is in [0.0094, 1] and u_ale in [0, 0.1], so beta is in (beta0 e^-(a+b+g), beta0].

P2 fit is identifiable at the observed u_ale scale. Synthetic check (360k pixels, K=40, true val parameters, u_ale mean 0.015, 12% undefined): fitted beta0 45.44 / a 0.350 / b 11.89 / g 0.049. Bootstrap std: b 0.06, beta0 0.07. With true b = 0, the fitted b is 0.2. LBFGS converges from init log 10. Caveat: the real pixels are correlated within views, and the 2 val scenes differ in u_ale scale (0.020 vs 0.007), so a scene-level confound in b cannot be tested without per-pixel data.

The P2 undefined indicator is rendered as the paper says. render_row marks u_ale_p undefined when D_p < 0.5 alpha_p and averages only the defined Gaussians. The fit (fit_adaptive) and the eval (adaptive_beta) use the same indicator. eval_seg refuses betas fit with another undef_frac. The fit uses covered pixels only, like the eval.

Freezing: freeze/frozen_on snapshot mu* (P0 and P2), A_d(kappa_post) mu* (P1), u_epi = 1/(1+s) and u_ale (NaN where undefined), which is exactly the paper's definition. Tensor sharing by torch.equal is safe: render_row does no in-place op, and the NaN channels are simply not shared, which costs memory only. ours_scalar has the same buffer and beta as P0 (35.98675), as expected, and is not a Table I row.

run_mapping restructure (vs 60d7796): the field gets the same inputs. The same full-resolution tokens are upsampled to (h, w), PCA-projected, and passed with num_pixels = h*w (ref = a0*240*320 = 7.68 px). Only the extraction order changed.

Ablation read-out copies (est_rbar / est_joint / est_legacy) share the same sums and change only the aleatoric estimator. mu* does not depend on the estimator, because kappa_hat always uses the joint form. r_tilde and the gates match the paper text.
NormLift 1 - C_inter: C_inter = ||F||/sum||R_v|| <= 1 (triangle inequality). An unseen Gaussian gets 1, and a one-view Gaussian gets 0 (biased toward certainty, as the paper says).
